Name: -1_sorrow_dear mother_father mother_beloved
Representative_Docs:
["1. Oh, it's been a long time, a long time  
Since I was at my father's,  
That path has already  
Grown over with blackthorn.  
2. Oh, it has grown over with blackthorn  
And wild rose hips,  
Where I used to pass  
When I was still a girl.  
3. Oh, I will take a scythe,  
Cut down the blackthorn,  
And with wings I will fly  
To my dear father.  
4. Oh, I will sit down, I will fall  
In the cherry orchard,  
On that bird cherry tree  
And I will sing.  
5. Oh, when I sing, –  
I will drown out the whole orchard,  
Oh, when I cry, –  
I will flood the whole orchard.  
6. And the old father  
Walks around the yard,  
He is leading his old mother  
By the hand.  
7. He is leading his old mother  
By the hand,  
And softly speaks  
To his daughters-in-law:  
8. – Get up, daughters-in-law,  
Listen to me,  
Is there something in our orchard  
Like a bird?  
9. – Oh, that’s not a bird,  
That is your daughter,  
She was born without happiness,  
She grew up without fate.  
10. She was born without happiness,  
She grew up without fate,  
She went away to a strange land  
And got married.  
11. And the strange land  
Rustles with the wind,  
The strange father doesn’t beat her,  
Doesn’t beat, but it hurts.  
12. The strange father doesn’t beat her,  
Doesn’t beat, but it hurts,  
The strange mother  
Harms her with words.  
13. The strange mother  
Harms her with words,  
She goes to the neighbor –  
Judges the daughter-in-law:  
14. – Lazy daughter-in-law,  
Does not want to work,  
She goes out to the field to reap,  
Then lies down and sleeps.  
15. She goes out to the field to reap,  
Then lies down and sleeps,  
She comes home –  
Her head hurts.", '1. Oh, I will go out on the hill,  
I will stand and look into the valley.  
2. I will stand and look into the valley  
At the red viburnum.  
3. On the red viburnum  
Is a little nightingale.  
4. The little nightingale  
Has a thin voice.  
5. Don’t chirp until dawn,  
Don’t cause me sorrow.  
6. Don’t cause me sorrow,  
Because I am in a foreign land.  
7. Because I am in a foreign land,  
I have no kin with me.  
8. No family,  
No faithful wife.  
9. I did not marry a wise woman,  
And I will not live with her.  
10. I will go to serve in the army,  
So that I don’t have to live with her.  
11. I have not yet served in the army,  
But I already married a wife.  
12. He covered her hands with cloth,  
And on top with his fist.  
13. He took his hat and went  
Out to the street to the girls.  
14. – Good evening to you, girls,  
I am left without a wife.  
15. All the girls said:  
– Hello, hello, Ivan!  
16. Only one remained silent,  
Turned around and left.  
17. She cried and left,  
Because she was the woman’s sister.  
18. – Good evening, our father,  
Your son-in-law is already having fun.  
19. Good evening, dear father,  
The son-in-law is at the party.  
20. – Let him have fun, daughter,  
God will punish him  
21. And also his family  
For our child.', '1. Oh, I will go up the hill,

Name: 0_cossack_black horse_horses_horse
Representative_Docs:
['1. – Young Cossack,  
Why are you sad?  
Have the oxen stopped,  
Or have you lost your way?  

2. – The oxen have not stopped,  
I have not lost my way,  
I loved a girl, –  
I am deeply sorrowful.  

3. I loved a girl,  
But I do not have her.  
Come out, girl,  
From the green grove.  

4. The Cossack went to the highland,  
The girl to the lowland...  
Oh, the Cossack became a thorn bush,  
The girl a guelder rose bush.  

5. The Cossack’s mother  
Went to pick thorn bushes,  
The girl’s mother –  
To break guelder rose branches.  

6. Oh, that is not a thorn bush, –  
That is your little son;  
Oh, that is not a guelder rose –  
That is your child.  

7. – Saddle up, Cossack,  
The black horse,  
We’ll sit and ride  
To the stranger priest.  

8. Oh, we arrived –  
The priest was not home:  
Is it your misfortune,  
Or my sorrow?  

9. Saddle up, Cossack,  
The black horse –  
We’ll sit and ride  
Into the open field.  

10. We’ll sit and ride  
Into the open field,  
Oh, there the girl  
Is weeding the wheat field.  

11. The wheat field,  
She is pulling out darnel,  
Throwing it  
Before the black horse’s feet.  

12. – Oh, stop, girl,  
Weeding the wheat,  
Weeding the wheat –  
Pulling out the darnel.  

13. Weeding the wheat,  
Pulling out the darnel,  
Throwing it  
Before the black horse’s feet.  

14. Oh, stop, girl,  
Pulling out the darnel –  
Spread a white bed,  
We will talk.  

15. We will talk,  
We will speak...  
The girl is afraid,  
Lest she betray.  

16. – Don’t be afraid, girl,  
Don’t be afraid of anything –  
The young Cossack  
Has betrayed no one.  

17. Oh, the girl  
Fell soundly asleep,  
The Cossack betrayed her,  
So she did not even hear.', '1. Oh, the young Cossack rode out  
To the steep mountain,  
Leaving his wife Maryana  
Adorned with her charms.  

2. Oh, the young Cossack rode out  
To go hunting,  
Set his black horse loose  
In the green grass.  

3. Set his black horse loose  
In the green grass,  
And he himself went to lie down and sleep,  
For he was filled with sorrow.  

4. Oh, the Cossack slept,  
He dreamed a dream,  
That from the right sleeve  
A falcon flew out.  

5. Whether from the right or the left  
The gray bird,  
It knows and finds out  
What is happening at home.  

6. Oh, as the young Cossack rose  
On his white feet,  
He ran from the mountain to the valley  
To the fortune teller.  

7. – Fortune teller, diviner,  
Guess this dream for me,  
That from the right sleeve  
A falcon flew out.  

8. – And I, young Cossack,  
Will interpret your dream,  
How could I not guess it?  
I will stake my head on it.  

9. Your wife Maryana  
Has given birth to a son,  
Only two hours left to daybreak,  
Her life has ended.  

10. When the young Cossack rode out  
To the steep mountain,  
There was no place to send her,  
Except to his home.  

11. When the young Cossack arrived  
Under the gate:  
– Come out, wife Maryana,  
Open the gates.  

12. Oh, Maryana did not come out,  
Out came her mother:  
– Greetings, greetings, young Cossack,  
You are no longer my son-in-law.  

13. Oh, when the young Cossack entered  
His own house,  
His faithful servants  
Were all in mourning.  

14. Oh, when the young Cossack entered  
The new chamber,  
His wife Maryana lay  
Dead as a stone.  

15. – Oh, get up, wife Maryana,  
Oh, get up, don’t lie down,  
The little son cried,  
Get up, and amuse him.', '1. Oh, a fire is burning on the mountain,  
Oh, a fire is burning on the mountain.  
2. And in the valley lies a Cossack,  
And in the valley lies a Cossack.  
3. He covered his eyes with an anthill,  
He covered his eyes with an anthill.  
4. His white face – with a handkerchief,  
His white face – with a handkerchief.  
5. And his little hands – with a whip.  
And his little hands – with a whip.  
6. And in his head a raven croaks,  
And in his head a raven croaks.  
7. And at his feet a grasshopper jumps,  
And at his feet a grasshopper jumps.  
8. – Don’t stand, horse, above me,  
Don’t stand, horse, above me,  
9. Don’t stomp the ground beneath you,  
Don’t stomp the ground beneath you,  
10. Because you won’t reach it,  
Because you won’t reach it.  
11. You can’t drink water from the sea,  
You can’t drink water from the sea.  
12. Run, horse, along the road,  
Run, horse, along the road.  
13. Along the beaten wide path,  
Along the beaten wide path.  
14. So that the Tatars don’t catch me,  
So that the Tatars don’t catch me.  
15. And don’t lift your saddle,  
And don’t lift your saddle.  
16. When you arrive at your father’s yard,  
When you arrive at your father’s yard.  
17. You will hit the palisade,  
You will hit the palisade.  
18. Your father will come out – will unsaddle you,  
Your father will come out – will unsaddle you.  
19. Your mother will come out – will untie you,  
Your mother will come out – will untie you.  
20. And she will ask about her son:  
And she will ask about her son:  
21. – Oh, you dark horse,  
– Oh, you dark horse,  
22. Where is my young son?  
Where is my young son?  
23. Did he die, or did he drown,  
Did he die, or did he drown,  
24. Or did he marry in a foreign land?  
Or did he marry in a foreign land?  
25. – He did not die, did not drown,  
– He did not die, did not drown.  
26. He married abroad.  
He married abroad.  
27. And he took himself a young lady, –  
And he took himself a young lady, –  
28. A grave in the open field.  
A grave in the open field.  
29. Take, mother, a handful of sand,  
Take, mother, a handful of sand,  
30. Sow it on the stone.  
Sow it on the stone.  
31. If that sand grows like rye,  
If that sand grows like rye,  
32. Then your son will return from the army.  
Then your son will return from the army.  
33. There is no rye sprouting from sand,  
There is no rye sprouting from sand,  
34. There is no son returning from the campaign,  
There is no son returning from the campaign,  
35. There is no sand – the wave washed it away,  
There is no sand – the wave washed it away,  
36. There is no son – a bullet killed him,  
There is no son – a bullet killed him.']

Name: 1_sorrow_beloved_orphan_fell love
Representative_Docs:
['1. I do not pity the little dog,  
Nor that little raven,  
Foolish reason carried me off  
To a foreign and distant land.  

2. And in that foreign land  
They will call me a drudge.  
They will tell me to cross  
A wide and deep river.  

3. Oh, I cannot swim across it,  
Nor can I get across it,  
Woe is me in a foreign land,  
Woe is me that I came here.  

4. Woe is me in a foreign land,  
Woe is me that I came here,  
A strange mother forces me  
To blow fire from a stone.  

5. – Do not mock me, strange mother,  
Do not mock me,  
Tie up my black eyes,  
Let me go for water.  

6. I walk through the meadow, singing a song,  
Oh meadows, spread out wide.  
I walk through the village, crying my sorrow, –  
Foreign girls, take comfort.  

7. Do not rejoice, foreign girls,  
There is a stone by the roadside,  
Fall upon it and gnaw it,  
Do not bring sorrow to my heart.  

8. Oh, I will go up the hill,  
Look down into the valley,  
There my beloved is grazing oxen,  
Still hurting in his bare feet.  

9. My little head aches,  
My forehead aches even more,  
Because of that girl,  
Whom I loved dearly.  

10. I loved her as a girl,  
I love her now as a young woman,  
And I will wait seven more years,  
To see if she will become a widow.  

11. I waited for her seven years,  
But she did not become a widow,  
Already, girl, my heart  
Has been torn apart into four.  

12. Oh, what good is my cattle to me?  
She owns the household,  
But my unworthy wife  
Will bring ruin to a good life.', '1. Oh, in the field  
A tall grave,  
On the grave  
A red viburnum.  

2. On the viburnum  
A black raven croaks,  
In a foreign land  
An orphan cries.  

3. – Oh, don’t croak, don’t croak,  
Black little raven,  
Oh, don’t cry, don’t cry,  
Poor little orphan.  

4. – Recently  
I became an orphan,  
For three years  
I have endured sorrow.  

5. Good people  
Advise me:  
– Get married,  
It will be easier for you.  

6. I got married,  
But don’t know to what,  
I fell in love  
With a worldly idler.  

7. I got married,  
But don’t know to whom,  
I fell in love  
With a bitter drunkard.  

8. I was drowning  
In a deep well,  
I was fighting  
With a bitter drunkard.  

9. Oh, don’t coo,  
Doves, in the house,  
Don’t wake  
My dear in bed.  

10. I know myself  
When to wake him up,  
When the sun  
Will be shining.  

11. I covered  
The middle window,  
So the sun wouldn’t burn  
My Cossack.  

12. – Get up, dear,  
My respect,  
Breakfast for you  
Is already ready.  

13. It stands  
In a green cup,  
A white towel  
Hangs on a little peg.  

14. Oh, my dear  
Started to get up from bed,  
The bed also  
Started to fly around the house.  

15. The bed started  
To fly around the house,  
My dear started  
To run away through the window.  

16. – Oh, my dear,  
Don’t you know jokes,  
That you are running away  
From me through the window?  

17. – I know, dear,  
I know your jokes, –  
For seven weeks  
I won’t get out of bed.  

18. But on the eighth  
I will get up,  
On the ninth  
I will go for a walk in the garden.', '1. Oh, there is a little lake in the field,  
There floated a little bucket,  
Pine wood staves, maple bottom,  
Let us not shun each other, my heart!  

2. If you shun me,  
People will laugh,  
Let’s join the right hands,  
And go to church to get married.  

3. Oh, we came to the church,  
But did not find the priest at home.  
Oh, is it yours, or is it mine  
Unhappy fate?  

4. – Oh, I would be glad to marry,  
To speak with you, my heart,  
The unloved one lies on my right hand,  
And I am afraid to wake him.  

5. Oh, there is a little lake in the field,  
There floated a little bucket,  
Pine wood staves, maple bottom,  
Let us not shun each other, my heart!  

6. There floated another one, too,  
Three days with water.  
– Come out, girl, come out, little fish,  
I want to talk with you!  

7. How can I come to you  
And talk with you?  
Oh, the unloved one lies on my right hand,  
And I am afraid to wake him.  

8. – Oh, my dear girl,  
Step away from the unloved one!  
I will kill the unloved one with a bow, like that dove,  
You, my dear girl!  

9. – Oh, whether you hit or miss,  
You will only separate me from him;  
Oh, whether you strike or not,  
You will only lose my life!  

10. You, young Cossack,  
You have a black horse,  
Saddle the horse, ride out of the yard,  
Because you are not mine, and I am not yours.  

11. The Cossack saddles the horse  
And speaks to the horse:  
– Trot, my horse, trot, black one,  
All the way to gentle Danube!  

12. When he arrives at the Danube,  
He stands, looks, and thinks:  
– Should I drown myself, or fall off the horse,  
Or return back?  

13. If I fall off the horse – I will be hurt,  
If I fall into the sea – I won’t live,  
If I return home,  
I will live – I will get married.']

Name: 2_servants_little wreath_wheat field_wreath
Representative_Docs:
['1. I was in the field for the harvest,  
In the collective farm for the reaping.  
2. The wreath swayed from the field  
All the way to the collective farm gate.  
3. – Come out, head, to us,  
Take a wreath from us.  
4. Take a wreath from us,  
And give us some for a dance.  
5. Take a flower from us,  
Give us some for a drink of vodka.  
6. We are young reapers,  
We have golden sickles.  
7. We reaped, did not rest,  
Finished harvesting the wheat.  
8. Our brigade is hardworking,  
Made straw from the stubble,  
9. The Malykiv lazy one,  
The wheat field stands still.  
10. Sell, head, the hen,  
Buy a barrel of vodka.  
11. Sell it with the chicks too,  
Settle accounts with the girls.', '1. The wreath rolled down from the field  
And under the collective farm gate,  
Under the collective farm doorstep,  
Give, head, some vodka.  
2. Don’t go, head, to the field,  
Because the stubble pricks in the field,  
They got lost among the sheaves,  
Like the moon among the stars.  
3. I am not afraid of the stubble,  
I will put on my shoes,  
I will watch the reapers.  
4. The little river flows, flows,  
The head is cooking fish,  
Looking out the window,  
Watching for the reapers.  
5. – My dear reapers,  
What were you doing in the field?  
Were you reaping or not reaping,  
Were you finishing the fields?  
6. The wife of the head, not fancy,  
Went outside the gate,  
Jingled the keys,  
Was watching for the reapers.  
7. The young foreman,  
Under him a black horse,  
Riding around the whole field,  
Watching for the reapers.  
8. The head is not at home,  
He went to Kyiv  
To buy some shots  
To treat the reapers.  
9. – Party, head, party,  
Sell the gray cow  
And the hen with chicks,  
Prepare a barrel of vodka.  
10. The wife of the head is different,  
She slaughtered a goose,  
And will also slaughter a goose  
As a snack for the reapers.', '1. Berries-blackberries,  
Collective farm harvests,  
Rye, wheat,  
So that they may be grand.  
2. The wreath rolled from the field  
Under the collective farm gate,  
Under the collective farm doorstep,  
Give me, chief, some vodka.  
3. – Don’t go, chief, to the field,  
Because the stubble in the field pricks,  
You’ll get lost among the sheaves,  
Like the moon among the stars.  
4. – I’m not afraid of the stubble,  
I will put on my boots,  
I will put on my boots,  
And watch the reapers.  
5. The river flows, flows,  
The chief is frying fish,  
Looking out the window,  
Watching for the reapers.  
6. – My dear reapers,  
What were you doing in the field:  
Were you reaping, or not reaping,  
Did you finish the fields?  
7. The chief’s wife, not beautiful,  
Came out behind the yard gate,  
Jingled the keys,  
Watching for the reapers.  
8. The chief is not at home –  
He went to Kyiv  
To buy shots of liquor –  
To treat the reapers.  
9. – Feast, chief, feast,  
Sell the gray cow  
And the hen with chicks too, –  
Prepare a barrel of vodka.  
10. The chief’s wife is not like that –  
She slaughtered a goose  
And will slaughter another goose  
For the reapers’ snack.  

Variant text:  
1. Berries-blackberries,  
Collective farm harvests,  
Rye, wheat,

2. The wreath rolls from the field

3. The young chief,

4. – Feast, chief, feast,

Name: 3_brothers_brother sister_brother_sister
Representative_Docs:

With curved horns,  
Hey, and I will plow a little field  
By the roadside.  
2. And I will sow wide hops,  
Hey, and I will brew  
Sweet beer.  
3. And I will brew sweet beer,  
Hey, and I will invite  
A distant kin.  
4. For the wealthy brother,  
I will send horses,  
Hey, and I will deliver them  
To the poor sister.  
5. The wealthy brother is already riding on horseback,  
Hey, and the poor sister  
Is going on foot.  
6. He sat the brother  
By the table,  
Hey, and the poor sister  
By the roadside.  
7. The wealthy brother  
Cuts little pies,  
Hey, and the poor sister  
Sheds tears.  
8. The wealthy brother  
Drinks mead-wine,

Sister, from the road.

A bowl of flour,

11. — Don’t you recognize me, brother,

12. Oh, one mother gave birth to us,  
Hey, but did not endow  
With the same happiness.', '1. And all the mountains are turning green,  
Where the rich rye is sown.  
2. Only one mountain is black,  
Where the poor widow sowed.  
3. Where she sowed, dragged,  
And moistened with her tears.  
4. A gray cloud came,  
Winter covered with snow.  
5. – My poor little head,  
Where will I spend the winter?  
6. Where will I spend the winter,  
When I don’t even have my own house?  
7. Oh, I will go to the Danube,

8. Winter sweeps with snow,

9. – Oh, brother, my dear,

10. – Oh, sister, little quail,

16. – Get up, father, get up from the grave,

17. Get up, dear father,  
You left behind tiny children.  
18. Get up, father, get up from the pit,  
It’s sorrowful to live near mother.  
19. – I will not get up, children, from the pit,  
Live yourselves near mother.
